theorem: Let R be the original trace18 PPT/SN3 5x5 grid of https://arxiv.org/html/2402.12966v1 Figure 2, independently PPT-checked in frontier-20261028-grid55-weighted-coordinate-theorem-v1.json SHA256 f1e892255a20d6c3b23afa42994a5fe90feea3be1cb63979a135e6da3ea702c6. For K|0,1,2,4>=|0,1,2,3>, K|3>=v0|0>+v1|1>, the actual Alice projection has SN<=2 whenever the explicit strict-denominator 3x3 Gram condition below holds. By source factor-swap symmetry the same applies to Bob, and an arbitrary opposite local map preserves the conclusion. In particular, |v0|^2<=1 and 3/4<=|v1|^2<=6/5 is a closed certified region containing genuine support-three kernel lines. This is not a global 4x4 result.
source_and_map: Use A=|02>+|11>+|20>, V=|01>, B=|12>+|34>, H=|14>, F=|32>; original weights are 1,1,1,1,2 respectively. Other grid generators and weights are listed in the predecessor. After the Alice map, A'=A, V'=V, B'=|12>+v0|04>+v1|14>, F'=v0|02>+v1|12>, H'=|14>. The kernel is span{|3>-v0|0>-v1|1>}. Source PPT and local congruence make the actual 4x5 output PPT.
seven_phase_seed: Assume v1!=0 and put s=1/(2*v1). Define vectors in the span (F',B',H') by L1=sF'+(1-v1*s)B'-v1*(1-v1*s)H', L2=v0*s B'+v0*(1-2*v1*s)H', L3=v0^2*s H'. For z^7=1 put q_z=A'+zV'+z^(-1)L1+z^(-2)L2+z^(-3)L3. Writing b(z)=(1-v1*s)z^(-1)+v0*s*z^(-2) and h(z)=-v1*(1-v1*s)z^(-1)+v0*(1-2*v1*s)z^(-2)+v0^2*s*z^(-3), q_z=A'+zV'+s*z^(-1)F'+b(z)B'+h(z)H'. Its first two Alice rows are [0,z,1+v0*s*z^(-1),0,v0*b(z)] and [0,1,b(z)+v1*s*z^(-1),0,v1*b(z)+h(z)]. The first is exactly z times the second for every nonzero complex z. The third row is |20> and the fourth is zero, so SR(q_z)<=2. The five phase exponents 0,1,-1,-2,-3 are distinct modulo7, so the phase average is [A']+[V']+[L1]+[L2]+[L3].
gram_condition: The residual on (F',B',H') is G=diag(2,1,1)-sum_(j=1)^3 t_j t_j^*, where t1=(s,1-v1*s,-v1*(1-v1*s)), t2=(0,v0*s,v0*(1-2*v1*s)), t3=(0,0,v0^2*s). Every combination of F',B',H' uses only Alice rows0,1 and thus has SR<=2. With U=|v0|^2,R=|v1|^2, the chosen s makes t2=(0,v0/(2v1),0), t3=(0,0,v0^2/(2v1)), and t1=(1/(2v1),1/2,-v1/2). Put dB=1-U/(4R), dH=1-U^2/(4R). If dB,dH>0, the rank-one Schur criterion is exactly 1/(8R)+1/(4*dB)+R/(4*dH)<=1. Under this condition G>=0 and the original state is the seven-phase SR2 average, a positive Gram sum and the untouched SR2 generators.
simple_uniform_subregion: If 0<=U<=1 and 3/4<=R<=6/5 then dB,dH>=2/3 and the Schur sum is at most 1/6+3/8+9/20=119/120<1. Thus this entire complex phase-invariant set satisfies the criterion. At v0=v1=1 the kernel span{|3>-|0>-|1>} has support3; the exact Gram pivots are [7/4,13/28,15/52].
opposite_side_and_weight_extension: The original source is invariant under swapping Alice and Bob, so the entire result transfers to the Bob chart. Any opposite local map preserves a nonnegative SR2 decomposition. The same upper bound also holds for R+T with T any nonnegative sum of the other ten original SR<=2 generator projectors; PPT of such an enlarged source must be checked separately.

exact_check.observed: At v=(1,1),(i,1),(1,i),(2,1), all forty 3x3 minors of q_z vanish as exact Gaussian-rational Laurent polynomials, all 400 entries of each actual Alice and Bob output match, and all actual PT checks pass. The first three residual Grams are PSD; the last is non-PSD and is only a negative control. The first local checker run omitted the three negative-degree phase projectors from its reconstruction and failed; they were added before the successful replay. It hash-pins/replays the previous trace24 ellipsoid checker. The all-complex claim is from the written phase/rank/Schur argument, not the finite samples.

limits: The Gram test and displayed subregion are sufficient only and cover a proper three-support kernel chart of this specific source and SR2-generator extensions. Other kernel directions, both generic maps, the unrestricted 4x4 PPT problem, an SN>=3 witness, independent/formal review and novelty remain open.
